newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA METALS - Global firms eye gold, diamond mines.
newsitem.headline: INDIA METALS - Global firms eye gold, diamond mines.

text.p: The lure of gold and diamonds has attracted more than 60 firms to the coastal Indian state of Orissa state in search of joint ventures to hunt for the precious metals, officials said on Wednesday.

"I can't recount a single day when I did not receive a telephone call from senior executives of global companies inquiring about the fate of their proposals," said Jagdish Prasad Dash, managing director of state-run Orissa Mining Corp (OMC).
Officials said several foreign and domestic firms were awaiting a tie-up with OMC to explore for gold and diamonds in the mineral-rich state.
Dash said investors want the state government to speed up the process for joint venture agreements even though some of them do not agree with the state's stipulated terms and conditions.
"The ball is now in the Orissa government's court," Dash told Reuters in an interview.

The Orissa government appointed OMC in 1994 as its agency to undertake exploration after an aero-magnetic survey by the Australian firm World Geo Science indicated the existence of rich reserves of gold, diamonds and gemstones.
OMC floated a global tender inviting bids for joint ventures for exploration. Some 61 foreign and domestic firms have so far responded, 40 for diamonds and 21 for gold, officials said.

Dash said last year the state government shortlisted five foreign companies, Australia's Cluff Resources Pacific NL, Kimberley Diamonds NL and Ashton Mining Ltd, Canada's Leader Mining Corp and South Africa's De Beers Prospecting Ltd, for diamond exploration.
He said OMC had already signed an agreement with Cluff Resources for exploration and downstream processing of alluvial diamonds in the state.

"Even a draft joint venture agreement has been prepared in consultation with (consultants) Price Waterhouse. We are waiting for the (state) government's nod for prospecting the designated areas," Dash said.
For joint ventures in gold exploration, OMC has shortlisted four companies, including three from overseas, Dash said.

The three foreign firms shortlisted were Australia's Empire Gold Mines Ltd (EGM), Canada's Dundee Bancorp Inc and Britain's Inter Continental Business Development Ltd. India's Manmohan Mineral Industries Pvt Ltd has also been shortlisted.
"EGM has agreed to explore and develop a mine in three to five years and to spend $300,000 during the first year," Dash said.
He said ICBD had agreed to spend $5.0 million over a five year period to cover exploration and development expenses but wanted a 60 percent equity stake.

Dash said most foreign firms want more than a 50 percent stake in the joint venture as well as management control. OMC was in favour of giving them management control but is reluctant to grant 50 percent equity.
A senior Orissa government official said a draft policy on gold and diamond mining by a high level committee has agreed to some of the suggestions by the foreign firms.
"Once the government approves the draft policy, we will go ahead with the joint venture agreements with the companies which agree to our terms and conditions," said Dash.
